accepted_upstream_counterexample: WP303 accepted test test_episode_and_process_require_distinct_minimum_lineage creates both an EPISODE TypedMemoryRecord and a PROCESS TypedMemoryRecord from the exact same MemoryLifecycleState. Therefore WP303 admits more than one valid TypedMemoryRecord identity for one (memory_id, lifecycle_generation).
product_negative: WP307 schema PRIMARY KEY(memory_id, lifecycle_generation) and write_record lookup by only that pair reject the second valid upstream record as MEMORY_GENERATION_ALREADY_BOUND_TO_DIFFERENT_BYTES. WP307 therefore narrows the accepted WP303 cardinality and invents a first-writer-wins typing authority not present in WP303.
required_discriminator: Create one lifecycle state; derive the accepted EPISODE and PROCESS records from that same state; persist both. Both exact record_sha256 identities must survive in the same canonical UnifiedDB and be independently readable/verified without one record replacing or vetoing the other.
failure_signature: Second valid WP303 record for the same memory_id/lifecycle_generation raises MEMORY_GENERATION_ALREADY_BOUND_TO_DIFFERENT_BYTES or cannot be independently read back by exact digest.
repair_constraint: Use exact TypedMemoryRecord identity (record_sha256) as the durable row identity. Lifecycle identity may be indexed but must not silently impose uniqueness. Any lifecycle-only read API must fail closed on ambiguity or require an exact expected digest; it must not choose one row arbitrarily. Preserve same-UnifiedDB, exact-byte, authority-receipt, main-schema, no-second-DB and inode-drift fences.
next_exact_action: Repair WP307 durable identity from lifecycle-pair uniqueness to exact record_sha256 identity, add the upstream EPISODE+PROCESS same-state regression, rerun WP307+WP303+WP206 repository CI, and only after an accepted exact-source result consider VPS fresh-process readback.
